paragraphs.text: Sun and Moon Korean is a Mumbai (Worli) Korean restaurant and kimchi brand selling small-batch fermented kimchi and K-fashion online alongside its dine-in restaurant. Teknoppy's goal was to shape the ecommerce storefront's content, product presentation, and SEO so the site could sell an unfamiliar product category — authentic Korean kimchi — to an Indian audience, while connecting the online store to the restaurant's existing reputation and media coverage.

rows.label: Key Services
rows.value: Ecommerce Content & SEO, Product Page Strategy, Website Optimization

paragraphs.html: Note: this case study is scoped to content, SEO, and product experience work — not full site development.

items.title: No educational product content
items.text: Kimchi varieties were listed without explanation, leaving first-time Indian buyers unsure what they were ordering or how it would taste.

items.title: Food and fashion blurred together
items.text: Kimchi and K-fashion products sat in the same undifferentiated catalog, without a clear separation between the two shop experiences.

items.title: No visible trust signals
items.text: Media coverage and customer reviews existed but weren't surfaced on the storefront, leaving an unfamiliar product category without third-party credibility at the point of purchase.

items.title: Educational product storytelling (directly answers Problem 1)
items.text: Each kimchi variety (Baechu, Oi, Pa, Baek, Yeolmu, Mu) carries its Korean name, phonetic English name, and a short flavor/benefit description, helping first-time buyers understand an unfamiliar product before they order.

items.title: Two clear shop categories (directly answers Problem 2)
items.text: Kimchi and K-fashion are separated into their own shop sections, so the site doesn't blur a food brand with a fashion catalog.

items.title: Trust signals from press and reviews (directly answers Problem 3)
items.text: Media coverage (Curly Tales, Pinkvilla Hallyutalk) and customer testimonials are surfaced on the homepage, giving an unfamiliar product category third-party credibility.

items.q: What was the main goal of the Sun and Moon Korean project?
items.a: To help a Mumbai Korean restaurant sell an unfamiliar product — authentic fermented kimchi — online, with content and SEO that educate first-time buyers and build trust.

items.q: What does Sun and Moon Korean sell online?
items.a: Small-batch fermented kimchi in five varieties, and Korean fashion (K-fashion), shipped from their Worli, Mumbai base.

items.q: Did the project affect Sun and Moon Korean's existing rankings?
items.a: The project was scoped to avoid keyword cannibalization against Sun and Moon Korean's existing product and category pages — no overlapping targets were introduced.

items.q: Does Sun and Moon Korean ship kimchi outside Mumbai?
items.a: The website lists Mumbai (Worli) as the base of operations; shipping coverage should be confirmed with the client before publishing.
